## Historical audit: S0150

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 of 2 and the text supplied here were audited; the referenced images were not independently inspected.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 22 [0,219267) | The stated goal was to reconstruct a 512×384 indoor photograph as editable SceneAct geometry, matching viewpoint, objects and appearance without using the photo as a texture. The request also supplied detailed construction and review procedures. No separate teacher message or teacher-authored diagnosis is identified in this visible chunk; receipt or adoption of any unseen teacher input is unknown. |
| Student history in line 22 [0,219267); student `model_response`, line 17 [0,11522) | The code constructs multiple owners: chaise, pillow, card, floor, architecture, curtain and foreground chair. Chaise frame, cushion, wings and trim are grouped; the pillow and card have separate poses and intended support. Colors, nine stripe tubes and cane rods approximate finishes and textures. These constructions and names do not independently establish visibility, physical contact or correct connections. |
| Student history in line 22 [0,219267) | After step 1, the student estimated the chaise was too small and changed camera lens 48→64 and target `(0,0,.88)`→`(.12,0,1)`, holding geometry and lighting fixed. Step 2 was reported successful. This is visible iterative exploration, though guided by the supplied procedure—not evidence of independent visual accuracy. |
| Student `model_response`, line 17 [0,11522); `execute`, line 18 [0,12186) | The student estimated remaining silhouette, wall/floor boundary and foreground-crop mismatches. It hypothesized excessive fill and executed a lighting-family revision: world strength .33→.16, window power 650→420 and fill 170→45, retaining the step-2 camera and scene. Predicted deeper shadows are a hypothesis, not a measured result. Pillow contact and head curvature were explicitly uncertain. |
| `execution_result`, line 19 [0,54005); `select`, lines 20–21 [0,59); student `model_response`, line 24 [0,355); `select`, line 25 [0,59) | Step 3 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected; after being supplied all three renders, the student replied `SELECT 3`. This establishes technical execution and selection, not geometric or visual correctness. Earlier steps 1 and 2 are reported successful in the line-22 history. |

**Outcome and lessons.** The visible outcome is a successful render and selection, with overall reconstruction correctness **unknown**, not a verified formal success or algorithm failure. A transferable practice demonstrated is separating camera and illumination revisions and recording predicted effects; a task-specific concern is the estimated cropped chair and misplaced wall boundary. Whether reduced fill actually improved the match, whether all parts touch correctly, and whether the final pose, materials and shadows match the photograph remain unresolved without independent image and geometry inspection. No empty patch or technical interruption is shown in this chunk.
